records.text: Paper card. Question: Can a rocksalt high-entropy oxide containing divalent Mn and Fe be synthesized and what are its properties?. System: (Mg,Mn,Fe,Co,Ni)O. Processing: bottom-up method using oxalate precursors, annealed at 1000°C for 6 hours in argon with MnO2 as an oxygen generator. Test conditions: various temperatures and atmospheres, including air, argon, and 5% H2/Ar. Findings: FeO-HEO has a single-phase rocksalt structure; cation site occupancy is highly random; metal ions are unanimously divalent; improved structural robustness compared to constituent binary oxides; antiferromagnetic order with a magnetic transition temperature of ~218 K. Mechanism: the oxygen sublattice acts as a buffer layer to accommodate different metal ions, and the cocktail effect contributes to the improved phase stability. Future work: dedicated study to determine the magnetic structure and correlations, and assessment of whether iron carries an orbital magnetic moment in this FeO-HEO. Quote: "a generic method was developed to synthesize rocksalt high-entropy oxides containing divalent manganese and iron"
